steps.text: In **A Black repertoire: replies to 1.e4 and 1.d4 that you can explain** you built a first Black line. After about twenty games, your games are data. Count what White played, then compare. On the Openings page (band 1100-1300) after 1.d4 d5, 2.Bf4 is the most common (19,063 of 71,413 games, 27%), then 2.c4 (25%), 2.Nf3 (16%), 2.e3 (12%), 2.Nc3 (11%). Your tally will differ, and the difference is information.

steps.prompt: An invented log of twenty games as Black after 1.d4 d5, to practise the tally: 2.Bf4 seven times, 2.Nf3 five times, 2.c4 three times, 2.e3 three times, 2.Nc3 once, 2.e4 once. Your notes cover only 2.c4 in depth. In how many of the twenty games did your notes not cover White's second move?

fields.label: Games not covered by my notes:

steps.text: **Three decisions from a tally.** *Deepen* a line you met often and handled badly (add a plan and one model position). *Trim* a line you prepared and never met. *Keep* a line that scored fine, even if you did not like it. **Rule of thumb:** twenty games is a small sample [H]; change a plan only when the same problem repeats, and spend memory only where one slip loses.

steps.title: A pawn is on offer
steps.prompt: You are Black and a pawn is on offer (or already won). Predict, then check.

After your next twenty games as Black, fill this in from your own games (the Openings page gives the comparison at your rating). Write what you changed and why, so you can check it after the following twenty.

steps.text: **Remember.** After about twenty games, count what White actually played and compare. Deepen a line you met often and handled badly, trim one you prepared and never met, keep one that scored fine. Twenty games is a small sample, so change a plan only when the same problem repeats, and spend memory only where one slip loses.
